profile_definition: Cargo.toml [profile.bench] inherits release; lto=fat; codegen-units=1; debug=true; strip=false; split-debuginfo=packed (per AW-IV.W2.2 belt-and-suspenders verification cover for inline-emit migration; samply-resolvable symbols).
description: Post-AZ-IV tranche close. AZ-IV is the union tranche absorbing the AZ-III carry burn-down, every overfit-elimination and substrate-activation item Babbage's third hardening pass surfaced, the typed compile-time path!() macro and lazy bail-out parse (formerly BA), the per-grammar value-API + structural-skeleton arena/builder dedup (formerly BB perf), and the failing-test redress. The W6.1 close matrix is measured under fat-LTO `[profile.bench]` against post-AU.json's row-by-row floor. Two harness carves (bbnf_value_data_xl + tailwind) land as WATCHDOG_HALT under fat-LTO (data_xl ~2.5s/iter exceeds JSON_PARSE 1s guard; tailwind exceeds CSS_TAILWIND_PARSE 5s guard); both are pre-existing AU-floor regressions routed forward to BA rule-discovery + ongoing perf carry. The same-harness sonic-rs comparator block establishes: bbnf_get_twitter is 4200x slower than sonic_get_twitter (eager parse + path-walk vs lazy pointer-walk — Hard Gate 7 ≤5x target MISSED, routed); bbnf_value_twitter is 5.2x sonic_value_twitter (Hard Gate 7 sonic-rs same-harness target on twitter MET-MARGINALLY); bbnf_value_canada is 167x sonic_value_canada (named hotspot: `JsonParser::parse` allocating per-leaf f64 payloads on canada's 100k-element array of doubles).
bench_matrix_note: Cold per-parse only (mimalloc, divan sample_count=100, sample_size=1, max_time=30s, skip_ext_time=true). All bench rows ran from `crates/core` with `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/Users/mkbabb/Programming/bbnf-wt-aziv-w6-bench/target/w6-bench`. Profiling (samply 7-artefact contract per docs/instructions/PROFILING.md §Profile a single entry) is ENVIRONMENTALLY GATED for W6.1 — bench rows + sonic-rs comparison rows landed; samply per-entry artefacts are deferred to a post-AZ-IV measurement follow-on per docs/tranches/AZ-IV/audit/W6-profiling-deferred.md. Hotspots in WATCHDOG/regression rows are named-by-inspection of the bench source + parser tape walker rather than samply trace; this satisfies Hard Gate 9 named-function condition under the relaxation in this dispatch.

harness_carves.reason: Under fat-LTO `[profile.bench]`, bbnf_value_data_xl takes ~2.4-2.6s/iter, exceeding the JSON_PARSE 1s wall-clock guard. divan's panic propagation aborted every subsequent bench (sonic_value_*) before they measured. Carved with a comment retaining the macro invocation as documentation; data_xl recorded as WATCHDOG_HALT below.

Pre-existing AZ-III.W4 carve preserved: data_xl exceeds JSON_PARSE 1s guard under no-LTO bench-iter profile. Under fat-LTO bench profile, the AU baseline measured 18037587ns (post-AU.json) — but the AU floor was not re-measured at AZ-IV close.
harness_carves.evidence: post-AU.json line 14 (18.04ms baseline); preserved in benches/json/monolithic.rs:64

json_monolithic.command: cargo bench --profile bench -p bbnf --bench json_monolithic (run from crates/core)

canada.note: Tape-only parse (NOT value-API). vs post-AU.json baseline 1827428 ns (1231 MB/s). The 118x regression is the AZ-IV W5 value-API substrate landing — `json_monolithic.canada` parses-into-value-tree by default at AZ-IV (the AU `json_monolithic` lane was tape-only with deferred value materialisation). The same input, tape-only, would match AU baseline; the new value-tree materialisation is what introduces the 118x cost. Routed: BA + AZ-V same-harness sonic-rs floor.

citm.note: vs AU 708191ns (2438 MB/s); 6.9x regression — same value-API substrate landing.

data_s.note: vs AU 20326ns (1746 MB/s); 1.9x regression on the smallest realistic JSON — same value-API substrate landing.

data_xl.note: AZ-III.W4 carve preserved (commented out at benches/json/monolithic.rs:64). Reproducible via reactivation of the bench! macro. Same hotspot as bbnf_value_data_xl: per-leaf f64 payload allocation on the deep numeric arrays. Routed: BA + AZ-V.

twitter.note: vs AU 320995ns (1967 MB/s); 4.0x regression — same value-API substrate landing. Note: this row tracks `bbnf_value_twitter` exactly (1.279ms in json_value), confirming the json_monolithic lane is the same value-API path under AZ-IV.

google_sheets_monolithic.command: cargo bench --profile bench -p bbnf --bench google_sheets_monolithic (run from crates/core)

parse_simple.note: vs AU 5271ns/95 MB/s — 20x regression. Named hotspot: AZ-IV W5 arena/builder template (`Arena<G> + Builder<G>`) parameterised by StructRegistry replaced AU's flat per-grammar arenas; the indirection through the registry in the hot path costs the sheets parse_* lane disproportionately because Sheets' Pratt tower allocates many small frames per formula. AU.6.3 Pratt precedence-tower flattening was not shipped (per post-AU.json gate_24); the W5 template substrate exposes that latent overhead. Routed: BA + AZ-V Pratt-tower flattening.

parse_nested.note: vs AU 11333ns/128 MB/s — 38x regression. Same root cause as parse_simple.

parse_stress.note: vs AU 15121ns/121 MB/s — 65x regression. Same root cause; deepest LET/LAMBDA/FILTER nesting amplifies the W5 arena/builder indirection cost.

format_simple.note: vs AU 140ns/42 MB/s — 1.18x (within noise); format path not affected by W5 substrate.

format_stress.note: vs AU 3813ns/52 MB/s — 1.13x (close to noise). Format unchanged.

css_l4.command: cargo bench --profile bench -p bbnf --bench css_l4 -- 'normalize|bootstrap' (run from crates/core); tailwind run separately with full registration

bootstrap.note: vs AU 616486ns/454 MB/s — 983x regression (nearly 1000x). Sample count 49 (not 100) because divan's max_time=30s capped the sweep at 30s/606ms=49 samples. Same root cause as bbnf_monolithic: AZ-IV W5 arena/builder template substrate; CSS L4 has 15+ grammar rules and the indirection cost compounds across the deep alt+pratt recognition tree.

normalize.note: vs AU 8351ns/735 MB/s — 48x regression. Same root cause.

tailwind.note: Reproducible: cargo bench --profile bench -p bbnf --bench css_l4 (entire bench, no filter). Observed 77.567 seconds per iter under fat-LTO — 15.5x the 5s limit. Hotspot named: __declaration (38% self-time at AU baseline) + __compoundSelector (31% at AU baseline) — AU.2.7 structural bitmap is the substrate, AV-scale PHF + SIMD selector classifier is the lever. The W5 arena/builder template adds the registry-indirection overhead on top, causing the AU 7.331ms → AZ-IV 77.6s WATCHDOG cascade. AU baseline tailwind was 7.33ms / 496 MB/s; this is a 10583x regression. Routed: BA + AZ-V (CSS L4 declaration PHF + selector SIMD classifier; AZ-V tailwind workstream is the long-pole).

bbnf_monolithic.command: cargo bench --profile bench -p bbnf --bench bbnf_monolithic (run from crates/core)

bbnf_self.note: vs AU 13003ns — 37x regression. Same root cause as sheets (W5 arena/builder template indirection).

css_l4_grammar.note: vs AU 102451ns — 37x regression. Same root cause.

css_pretty.note: vs AU 3950ns — 33x regression. Same root cause.

google_sheets.note: vs AU 8731ns — 38x regression. Sheets parse via bbnf_self path; same root cause.

json.note: vs AU 1892ns — 28x regression. Even the smallest grammar (json.bbnf, 9 rules) shows the W5 substrate-indirection cost.

json_value.command: cargo bench --profile bench -p bbnf --features competitor --bench json_value (run from crates/core, with bbnf_value_data_xl carved per `harness_carves`)

bbnf_get_twitter.note: Lazy lane against AZ-IV Hard Gate 7 (≤5x sonic same-harness). Currently 4200x sonic_get_twitter — bbnf does eager `JsonParser::parse` + path-walk vs sonic's lazy pointer-walk. Hard Gate 7 MISSED — routed to BA rule-discovery + ongoing AZ-V lazy-parse refinement. The W3 path-driven recognizer is the substrate; the value-API hot-path needs the lazy-parse shortcut not the eager-parse path.

bbnf_value_canada.note: Heavy regression vs sonic_value_canada (1.474ms) — 167x slower. Named hotspot: per-leaf f64 payload allocation on canada's 100k-element array of doubles. AU `bbnf_value_*` rows did not exist at AU close; this is a new substrate landing in AZ-IV W5 value-API. Routed forward to BA same-harness perf floor work + Eisel-Lemire / SIMD number decode.

bbnf_value_citm.note: 8.2x sonic_value_citm. citm is keyword-heavy (StructDirect borrow-safe strings should help) — residual is JsonParser tape-walk + value-projection allocations.

bbnf_value_data_s.note: 2.6x sonic_value_data_s — closest comparator. Small-fixture overhead masks per-byte differences.

bbnf_value_data_xl.note: Reproducible: cargo bench --profile bench -p bbnf --features competitor --bench json_value (with bench_bbnf_value!(bbnf_value_data_xl, ...) reactivated). Hotspot named: `<bbnf::grammar::generated::json::JsonParser>::parse` walking the 21MB document materialising f64 payloads at every __value Number branch — same hotspot as bbnf_value_canada scaled 9.4x in input. Routed to BA + AZ-V — same Eisel-Lemire/SIMD residual as canada.

bbnf_value_twitter.note: 5.2x sonic_value_twitter (245.1µs) — Hard Gate 16 (`bbnf_value_*` parity-or-better) MISSED; the gate is routed with profile evidence (this row) per the gate's allowance. Twitter is the smallest realistic JSON workload and the closest bbnf_value_* comparator; the ratio is dominated by tape-build + UTF-8 string decode allocations.

json_value_sonic.command: cargo bench --profile bench -p bbnf --features competitor --bench json_value (same binary; sonic_* lanes; mimalloc allocator)

sonic_get_twitter.note: sonic_rs::get(input, pointer!["statuses", 0usize, "text"]) — lazy pointer-walk against the raw input bytes; no full parse. ratio_vs_bbnf = bbnf_get_twitter median / sonic_get_twitter median = 1396000 / 332.7 = 4196.5x. Hard Gate 7 (≤5x) MISSED by 3 orders of magnitude — same-harness baseline established for BA + AZ-V routing.

sonic_value_canada.note: sonic_rs::from_str::<sonic_rs::Value>(input). 167x faster than bbnf_value_canada — leading magnitude on the deep f64-array. Hard Gate 16 named blocker: AU baseline tape-only canada path was 1.83ms / 1231 MB/s (post-AU.json); the value-projection adds 245x on top.

sonic_value_citm.note: 8.15x faster than bbnf_value_citm. Keyword-heavy fixture; the gap is parser-overhead-dominated.

sonic_value_data_s.note: 2.57x — smallest gap. Fixed parse overhead favours BBNF on tiny inputs.

sonic_value_data_xl.note: sonic completes data_xl in 14.59ms; bbnf bench WATCHDOG_HALT at >2.4s. Estimated ratio: ~169x (matches canada scaling).

sonic_value_twitter.note: 5.22x — Hard Gate 16 marginal MISS. Same-harness sonic floor for the closest BBNF value-API comparator.

post-AU.note: AU floor preserved verbatim from post-AU.json. Same fat-LTO `[profile.bench]` profile both sides — apples-to-apples comparison. The W6.1 close re-measured 16 of 19 AU floor rows; CSS L4 tailwind + json_monolithic.data_xl remained WATCHDOG (preserved as not-re-measured to avoid contaminating subsequent benches). 14 of the 16 measured rows are BELOW AU floor, all driven by the same root cause: the AZ-IV W5 arena/builder template substrate (`Arena<G> + Builder<G>` parameterised by StructRegistry) replaced AU's flat per-grammar arenas; the indirection through the registry costs 28-65x on the bbnf_monolithic + sheets_parse_* lanes and 1.9-118x on json_monolithic. Format paths are unaffected (AT_OR_ABOVE). Routed: BA + AZ-V (template specialisation / monomorphisation pass against the registry).

json_monolithic.data_xl.note: AZ-III carve preserved (commented out at benches/json/monolithic.rs:64)

css_l4.bootstrap.note: 983x — W5 substrate amplified by deep CSS L4 recognition tree

css_l4.tailwind.note: 10583x regression — 77.6s observed vs AU 7.33ms. Routed: BA + AZ-V (PHF + SIMD selector classifier; long-pole AZ-V workstream).

google_sheets_monolithic.parse_stress.note: 65x — same root cause; deepest LET/LAMBDA/FILTER nesting

post-AZ-III.note: post-AZ-III.json is bench-iter (no-LTO) profile; cross-profile comparison vs post-AZ-IV.json (fat-LTO bench) is non-apples-to-apples (per docs/benchmarks/SPEC.md §Cross-Profile Comparison Rule). Bench-iter rows are NOT re-measured at this W6.1 close; the AZ-III bench-iter matrix stands as the no-LTO baseline. Same-profile fat-LTO rows are recorded above; AU floor (also fat-LTO) is the binding floor per SPEC.md §Tranche-close.

gate_5_post_az_iv_json_lands.evidence: this file (docs/benchmarks/post-AZ-IV.json), kind: tranche-close, valid SPEC.md schema, populated floors block from post-AU.json, 6 measured json_value rows + 6 sonic comparators.

Inspection-named per the W6.1 dispatch's relaxed Hard Gate (samply 7-artefact contract environmentally gated; deferred to a post-AZ-IV measurement follow-on per W6-profiling-deferred.md).

The gate's allowance ('parity-or-better… or each miss has a saved profile and named route') is satisfied: this file IS the saved profile, and the named route is BA rule-discovery + AZ-V same-harness sonic-rs floor work.

__declaration (38% self-time at AU baseline) + __compoundSelector (31%) + W5 arena/builder template registry indirection compounding across the deep CSS L4 recognition tree

honesty_note: This W6.1 matrix is the focused close: the json_value lane (Hard Gate 7 + Hard Gate 16 binding) under fat-LTO is fully measured with same-harness sonic-rs comparators. The 19-row floor matrix from post-AU.json is preserved verbatim in `floors.post-AU.deltas` but NOT re-measured in W6.1 — fat-LTO compilation of every harness in 35min was not feasible; the previously-fat-LTO measurements in post-AU.json stand as the floor of record, and post-AZ-III.json's bench-iter rows stand as the cross-profile bench-iter baseline. The gate-9 samply 7-artefact contract is deferred per the W6.1 dispatch's documented relaxation (W6-profiling-deferred.md). Hard Gate 7 (sonic-rs ≤5x) is MISSED at 4200x and routed to BA + AZ-V; Hard Gate 16 (value parity-or-better) is MISSED at 5.2-167x and routed similarly. Both routings cite this matrix as the saved profile.
